properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 28 at 4:44PM CDT until October 28 at 5:00PM CDT by NWS Twin Cities/Chanhassen MN
properties.description:
At 444 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located over Brunswick, or
16 miles north of Cambridge, moving east at 50 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Ogilvie, Lewis Lake, Mora, Brunswick, Grandy, Stanchfield and
Grasston.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

A Tornado Watch remains in effect until 900 PM CDT for a portion of
east central Minnesota.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued October 28 at 3:42PM MDT until October 28 at 6:45PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
FFWEPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Otero County in south central New Mexico...

* Until 645 PM MDT.

* At 342 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of South Central Otero County.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
properties.sender: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM

properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 28 at 4:39PM CDT until October 28 at 5:00PM CDT by NWS Twin Cities/Chanhassen MN
properties.description:
At 439 PM CDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from
over Lakeville to over Dundas, or along a line from 15 miles north of
Northfield to 5 miles southwest of Northfield, moving northeast at 40
mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

This severe thunderstorm will be near...
Lakeville, Farmington and Northfield around 440 PM CDT.
Dundas and Burnsville around 445 PM CDT.
Rosemount and Apple Valley around 450 PM CDT.
Inver Grove Heights and Eagan around 455 PM CDT.

Other locations impacted by the severe thunderstorm include Lakeville
Airport, Castle Rock, Randolph, Hampton and Coates.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. These storms are capable of producing damaging winds and
large hail.

A Tornado Watch remains in effect until 900 PM CDT for portions of
east central and south central Minnesota.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued October 28 at 3:25PM MDT until October 28 at 6:30PM MDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
FFWMAF

The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Eddy County in southeastern New Mexico...

* Until 630 PM MDT.

* At 325 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. The expected rainfall rate is 1
to 1.5 inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Carlsbad Caverns National Park.
properties.instruction:
In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued October 28 at 5:19PM AST until October 28 at 6:45PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
SMWSJU

The National Weather Service in San Juan has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N...

* Until 645 PM AST.

* At 519 PM AST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located over open waters of Atlantic Waters of
Puerto Rico and USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N zone, moving north at 10
knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 34 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters of Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from
10 NM to 19.5N.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.
Wind gusts 34 knots or greater, high waves, dangerous lightning, and
heavy rain are possible with this storm.

Frequent lightning is occurring with this storm. If caught on the
open water stay below deck if possible, keep away from ungrounded
metal objects.
properties.area: Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico AND USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued October 28 at 4:45PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N...
Coastal Waters of Northern Puerto Rico out 10 NM...

* At 445 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated a strong thunderstorm,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. This strong
thunderstorm was located over open waters of Atlantic Waters of
Puerto Rico and USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N and Coastal Waters of
Northern Puerto Rico out 10 NM zones, moving north at 10 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters of Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from
10 NM to 19.5N and Coastal Waters of Northern Puerto Rico out 10
NM.
properties.instruction:
Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, lightning strikes, and heavy downpours. Funnel clouds are
possible. Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this
storm passes.
properties.area: Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico AND USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N; Coastal Waters of Northern Puerto Rico out 10 NM

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 28 at 11:51AM MDT until October 30 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Grande at Embudo affecting Rio Arriba and Taos Counties.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Embudo.

* WHEN...Until Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Minor overbank flows are occurring above the
Embudo gaging site. Access to riverside picnic facilities above
Pilar and below the Taos Junction Bridge along State Route 570 will
be limited if further rises occur. Water may be extremely close to
underside of bridge over Rio Grande on Aguas Caliente Rd in Pilar.
Other localized effects due to the high water levels will begin to
be felt at a stage of 10 feet but no significant flooding is
expected until the river rises to 12 feet.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Wednesday the stage was 7.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.1 feet
tomorrow morning.
- Action stage is 8.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 11:45AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Chama Below Chamita affecting Rio Arriba County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Chama below Chamita.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, Properties in the flood plain along the Rio
Chama and near the junction of the Rio Ojo Caliente will see water
in their yards. Impacts can include bank erosion and damage to
wells and septic tanks.  These impacts will increase in severity at
higher river levels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Wednesday the stage was 6.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:00 AM MDT Wednesday was 6.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain between 6.4 and 6.7
feet through the next several days.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.7
feet on 07/21/2009.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 9:03AM EDT until October 29 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Upstream persistent gusty northeast winds and tidal effects on the
St John River are slowing flow. At Deland, the river is forecast to
crest near Minor Flood Stage the next couple days, then begin a slow
decline through Action Stage later in the week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Docks and piers are completely submerged at
Pier 44 Marina. Many docks are partially submerged at Hontoon
Landing Marina.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 4.0 feet
the next couple days. It will then fall below flood stage late in
the week.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 1215 AM EDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 8:58AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent gusty northeast winds and upstream tidal effects are
slowing river flow on the St Johns River at Astor. River levels are
forecast to begin a slow decline late this week, but remain in
Moderate Flood stage for at least the next couple weeks.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland, Astor...Moderate flooding
is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 3.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...River levels are forecast to crest around 3.8 feet
this week, then begin a gradual decline late in the week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 200 AM EDT.
